m:spaccanapoli: Free to walk. The nativity-scene workshops are open all year, but from mid-November to 6 January the street is packed. Watch out for scooters squeezing past and for pickpockets in the crowd.
m:sansevero: Full ticket €12 (reduced €8 for ages 18–26, €6 for 10–17), limited entry: book online on museosansevero.it. Open 9am–7pm (last entry 30 minutes before), closed on Tuesdays; in summer it sometimes opens on Tuesdays too. No photos inside. Prices and hours from an August 2026 guide: to be confirmed.
m:santachiara: Cloister and museum €7 (reduced €5), open Monday–Saturday 9:30am–5pm and Sunday 10am–2pm, last entry 30 minutes before. The basilica is free, open 7:45am–12:45pm and 4:40–8pm (hours from an August 2026 guide, to be confirmed).
m:piomonte: Ticket €10 (reduced €8), open Monday–Saturday 10am–6pm and Sunday 9am–2:30pm. Hours and price from an online listing, to be confirmed.
m:duomo: According to an August 2026 guide the cathedral is open every day 9:30am–5pm with visits at fixed times, free but by booking; the Chapel of the Treasure has free entry with a break at midday; the Treasure Museum costs €15 with audio guide (9:30am–6pm, last entry 5pm). Hours and rules to be confirmed on the Diocese website.
m:mann: Full ticket €20 (reduced €2 for EU citizens aged 18–25, free under 18): you'll find it on the official website cultura.gov.it. Open 9am–7:30pm, ticket office until 6:30pm, closed on Tuesdays. On the first Sunday of the month entry is free, but it's crowded. Data from the Ministry of Culture website.
m:plebiscito: The square and the gallery are always accessible and free. Inside the Galleria there are shops and cafés, and nearby is the Gran Caffè Gambrinus, a historic café since 1860.
m:reale: Full ticket €15 (ages 18–24 €2, free under 18). Open every day 9am–8pm (last entry 7pm), closed on Wednesdays. The Romantic Garden is free 9am–7pm. Data from the Ministry of Culture website.
m:castelnuovo: Ticket €6 (free under 18). Open Monday–Saturday 8:30am–5pm (ticket office closes an hour earlier) and Sunday until 2pm: the rooms sometimes close earlier, check at the entrance. Hours and price from a March 2026 online listing, to be confirmed.
m:ovo: Entry to the castle is free. Summer hours are normally 9am–7:30pm on weekdays and 9am–2pm on Sundays, shorter in winter: the castle can close for events at short notice. The Via Partenope seafront is always free. Data from guides, to be confirmed.
m:sanmartino: Full ticket €6 (ages 18–25 €2, free under 18). Open 8:30am–6:30pm (last entry 5:30pm), closed on Tuesdays; the gardens close an hour earlier. Data from the Ministry of Culture website.
m:sotterranea: Ticket €10, a tour of about two hours at fixed times (normally at 10am, noon, 2pm and 4pm, from a 2024 guide). The route has narrow passages and a temperature of about 17 degrees: bring a jacket. Book your time online. Hours and price to be confirmed.
m:quartieri: Free to walk. By day and in the early evening it's lively; late at night avoid deserted alleys. Keep your bag and phone in front and watch out for scooters.
vd:scaturchio: A historic 1903 pâtisserie in the old centre, on Piazza San Domenico Maggiore: sfogliatelle, babà, the «Ministeriale» chocolate sweet and coffee at the counter.
vp:scaturchio: A coffee and a sfogliatella at the counter stay under €5 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mexico: A historic bar on Piazza Dante where Neapolitans have their coffee standing at the counter: creamy, already sweetened and very strong. Pay first at the till and take the receipt to the barista.
vp:mexico: A coffee costs about €1.20–1.50 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:dimatteo: A historic pizzeria on Via dei Tribunali, known for fried pizza and the cuoppo, a paper cone of fried snacks. Take a number and wait outside; the tables are cramped and you eat quickly. Closed on Sundays.
vp:dimatteo: A margherita costs about €5–6; with a drink you stay under €10 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:portalba: Naples' oldest pizzeria, open since 1738 under the Port'Alba arch, among the bookshops of Piazza Dante: classic Neapolitan pizza, calzone and seafood dishes in a large room.
vp:portalba: A margherita costs about €7–8; with a beer it's around €12 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:michele: An 1870 pizzeria, famous from the film «Eat Pray Love», that makes only two pizzas: margherita and marinara. Since 2020 you queue with a number handed out at the entrance. Closed on Sundays.
vp:michele: A pizza costs about €6–7; with a drink it's around €10 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:attanasio: A short walk from the station, the pâtisserie selling hot ricotta sfogliatelle straight from the oven, riccia (flaky) or frolla (shortcrust), often with a queue. Always a good way to start or end a day in Naples.
vp:attanasio: A sfogliatella costs about €2.50–3 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:gambrinus: Naples' historic café since 1860, next to the Royal Palace and the San Carlo Theatre: rooms with mirrors and stucco, pastries and coffee at the counter, cheaper than at a table.
vp:gambrinus: At the counter a coffee and a sfogliatella stay under €6; at the tables prices are higher (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:sfmary: A small kiosk-pâtisserie inside the Galleria Umberto I, famous for hot sfogliatelle and sweets to take away: eaten standing under the dome.
vp:sfmary: A sfogliatella costs about €2.50–3 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:nennella: A noisy, cheerful trattoria in the Quartieri Spagnoli, with waiters who sing and joke and hearty Neapolitan dishes such as pasta e patate, ragù and meatballs. You eat at long shared tables.
vp:nennella: Budget range; a full meal stays under €20 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:brandi: The pizzeria where the margherita is said to have been born in 1889, in an alley near the Royal Palace: wood-fired oven and a room with period photos.
vp:brandi: A pizza costs about €8–10; with a drink it's around €15 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:starita: A pizzeria in the Materdei district, off the tourist trail, open since 1901: the fried «montanara» pizza is its classic. Take a number; the wait is long at dinner.
vp:starita: A pizza costs about €6–8; with a drink it's around €11 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:concettina: A pizzeria in the Rione Sanità, Totò's neighbourhood, with soft dough and local ingredients such as Vesuvius tomatoes. It's one of the favourite places for Neapolitans who want to eat well without spending much. Closed on Sundays.
vp:concettina: A pizza costs about €7–9; with a drink it's around €13 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:chaletciro: An ice-cream parlour and pâtisserie on the little harbour of Mergellina, from breakfast until late: ice cream, tartufo and sfogliatelle to eat while strolling along the seafront.
vp:chaletciro: An ice cream costs about €3–5 (from reviews). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:capodimonte: Caravaggio, Titian and Raphael in a Bourbon palace on the hill, with a park.
cd:catacombe: An early Christian necropolis on two levels, with frescoes and tombs, explored with a guide.
cd:zevallos: The Martyrdom of Saint Ursula, Caravaggio's last painting, in a palace on Via Toledo.
cd:madre: The contemporary art museum, with works by Kapoor and Kounellis.
cd:girolamini: A Baroque church with a cloister and a picture gallery, next to the cathedral.
cd:sancarlo: Europe's oldest opera house, with gilded boxes.
cx:sancarlo: Tours are at fixed times and depend on rehearsals.
cd:orto: A 19th-century garden with tropical plants and glasshouses.
cd:tesoro: The treasure of jewels, silver and relics given to the saint over the centuries.
cd:borbonico: An 1850 Bourbon tunnel dug into the tuff, used as a shelter during the war.
cx:borbonico: Guided visits only, at fixed times.
cd:dohrn: Europe's oldest aquarium, in the Villa Comunale.
